title: NG6: Corollary 1 (ill-posedness) over-reaches; explicit bound x_e <= 2d+1 makes per-diameter enumeration finite (supplies G3)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, Proposition 1 / Corollary 1 (lines 295-302) and the "On the figure 5376" section.

**The gap.** Corollary 1 declares the problem has "no finite answer," because the uniform-odd family yields infinitely many geodetic homeomorphs of UNBOUNDED diameter. But the problem's own parameter is a FIXED diameter $d$ ("geodetic graphs of diameter $d\ge 2$"), and for fixed $d$ the solution set is FINITE, via an elementary a priori bound the solution never states:
$$\boxed{\,x_e\le 2d+1\quad\text{for every edge }e.\,}$$

**Proof of the bound.** Let $p$ be the interior point of $e=ab$ at offset $r=\lfloor x_e/2\rfloor$. For every vertex $u\notin e$, any $p$-$u$ path exits $e$ through $a$ or $b$, so
$$d_{G'}(p,u)=\min\big(r+d_{G'}(a,u),\,(x_e-r)+d_{G'}(b,u)\big)\ \ge\ \min(r,\,x_e-r)=\lfloor x_e/2\rfloor,$$
using $d_{G'}(\cdot,u)\ge 0$. Off-$e$ vertices exist (e.g. any branch vertex $\ne a,b$), so $\mathrm{diam}(G')\ge\lfloor x_e/2\rfloor$, giving $x_e\le 2d+1$.

**Consequence.**
1. The infiniteness is purely an artefact of letting $d\to\infty$; per fixed diameter $d$ the enumeration is WELL-POSED and finite, so Corollary 1's "ill-posed / no finite count" verdict is an over-reach as stated. (The problem's "$d\ge 2$" most naturally reads as: enumerate for each diameter, each finite.)
2. This is exactly the explicit length bound demanded by carried-over gap **G3 (rm-05346-4)**, which the solution otherwise leaves unaddressed (it asserts infiniteness instead of bounding).

**What it does NOT fix.** Practicality. Even the bounded search has $(2d+1)^{175}$ leaves -- astronomically large already for $d=2$ -- so the problem's "practical (real) running time" demand (gap G4 = rm-05346-5) and the unsound-pruning gap NG4 (rm-05346-10) remain open. A genuine enumeration must collapse this via constraint propagation and $\mathrm{Aut}(H)$ symmetry (order $252000$), with an honest runtime model.

**Bonus for G1.** Under fixed $d$, condition (G) involves only offsets $\le 2d+1$ and distances $\le d$, so it becomes a FINITE system of linear inequalities -- the natural setting in which to reconcile (or refute) the problem's "$5376$ equations," rather than dismissing the local system via the absent check.py (NG3).
